# ops

Machine setup for the nightly job and the database on the owner's Mac. Nothing here is imported by the app; `backup.sh` is called by `src/ingest/cli-nightly.ts`, the rest is run by hand.

## Files
| File | What it's for |
|---|---|
| `install-nightly.sh` | Installs (or reinstalls) the launchd agent: fills in the paths in the plist template, lints it, `launchctl bootout` then `bootstrap`. Safe to re-run. |
| `com.tradesence.nightly.plist` | Template for the agent: `bun run ingest:nightly`, Mon–Fri 19:30 local, log to `~/Library/Logs/tradesence-nightly.log`. `__BUN__`, `__REPO__`, `__LOG__` are rewritten by the installer; never install the template as is. |
| `backup.sh` | One `pg_dump` (custom format) per night into `~/Backups/tradesence` (newest 7 kept), plus a copy to iCloud Drive (newest 3). Also `bun run db:backup`. Env knobs: `TRADESENCE_BACKUP_DIR`, `_KEEP`, `_MIRROR` (empty turns iCloud off), `_MIRROR_KEEP`, `_MIRROR_TIMEOUT`. |
| `postgres-tuning.sql` | `ALTER SYSTEM` settings (memory, SSD cost) for this machine; applied by hand as superuser, then restart Postgres. |

## Rules here
- launchd's PATH has no `bun` and no `pg_dump`: the plist gets bun's absolute path from the installer, and `backup.sh` sets its own PATH (Postgres 14 first). Keep it that way.
- `backup.sh` writes `*.partial` and renames, so a dump that dies half-way is never mistaken for a good one; the iCloud folder is only touched by exact path (listing it hangs from launchd), tracked in `.mirrored` in the backup dir.
- A failed iCloud copy is a warning, never a failure; the local copy is the one that matters. The script stops adding iCloud copies after 3 nights of failed deletions.
- `backup.sh` reads `DATABASE_URL` from the repo's `.env` when not set; never print or log it.
- The backup runs last in `cli-nightly.ts` so it includes tonight's data; its exit code only produces a warning.
